questions.question: According to Census 2011, which among the following has the minimum population density?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh** has the **minimum population density **according to **Census 2011.**
 
• The population density of Arunachal Pradesh is **17 persons per square kilometer.**
 
• **Chandigarh**, on the other hand, has the** highest population density** among given options with **9252 persons per square kilometer.**
 
• **Andhra Pradesh** has a population density of **308 persons per square kilometer **and **Sikkim **has a population density of **86 persons per square kilometer.**
 
• **Population density** is the number of **people living** in a particular **area per unit of land.**
 
• It is an important indicator of the **level of development and resource use **in a region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandigarh** is a **Union Territory **and a** city **that serves as the **capital **of the states of **Punjab and Haryana.**

 
 
• It is one of the** most planned cities** in India and has a high standard of living.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh** is a state in southern India with a population of over **49 million.**
 
 
• It is the **seventh-largest state** in India by area and the** tenth-largest by population.**
 
 
 
• **Sikkim** is a state in **northeastern India **and is the least populous state in the country.
 
 
• It is known for its natural beauty and is a **popular tourist destination.**

questions.question: According to Census 2011 of India, which Union Territory has the second highest percentage of urban population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandigarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census 2011, Chandigarh has the second highest percentage of urban population among Union Territories in India.
 
• Chandigarh has an urban population percentage of 97.25%.
 
• Chandigarh is a city and a union territory in India that serves as the capital of the two neighboring states of Punjab and Haryana.
 
• The city was designed by the Swiss-French modernist architect, Le Corbusier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi**:

 
 
• Delhi has the highest percentage of urban population among Union Territories, with 97.50% as per Census 2011.
 
• It is the capital territory of India and a significant cultural, political, and commercial center.
 
 
 
• **Puducherry**:
 
 
• Puducherry, formerly known as Pondicherry, has an urban population of 68.33%.
 
• It comprises four coastal regions: Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam.
 
 
 
• **Daman and Diu**:
 
 
• Daman and Diu had an urban population percentage of 75.16% as per the 2011 Census.
 
• In January 2020, Daman and Diu were merged with Dadra and Nagar Haveli to form the new union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
 
 
 
• **Union Territories in India**:
 
 
• Union Territories (UTs) are regions governed directly by the Central Government of India.
 
• As of 2023, India has 8 Union Territories, which include Delhi, Puducherry, Chandigarh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Ladakh, and Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.question: According Census 2011 of India, which of the following union territories has the second highest literacy rate?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Daman and Diu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census 2011 of India**, the **Union Territory** of **Daman and Diu** has the **second highest literacy rate** among the Union Territories.
 
• The literacy rate of **Daman and Diu** is recorded at **87.07%**, which places it just below Lakshadweep, the Union Territory with the highest literacy rate.
 
• **Daman and Diu** are located on the western coast of India and were a part of the Portuguese territories in India until 1961.
 
• The high literacy rate in this region can be attributed to efforts in promoting education and the availability of basic educational infrastructure.
 
• Post the **merger of Daman and Diu with Dadra and Nagar Haveli in January 2020**, they now form a single Union Territory.
 
• The Union Territory has a relatively small population, which has contributed to effective implementation of educational policies and initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lakshadweep**__

 __
 
• **Lakshadweep** has the **highest literacy rate** among the Union Territories as per the **Census 2011**, recorded at **91.85%**.
 
• The Union Territory consists of a group of **36 small islands** and is located in the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• The high literacy rate is due to the consistent educational efforts and literacy programs implemented by the government.
 
 
 
• **Chandigarh**__
 __
 
• Chandigarh, a Union Territory and the capital of both **Punjab and Haryana**, has a literacy rate of **86.05%**.
 
• The city is known for its planned urban infrastructure and strong emphasis on education.
 
• It houses several prestigious educational institutions, such as **Panjab University**.
 
 
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__
 
 
• The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, located in the Bay of Bengal, have a literacy rate of **86.63%**.
 
• The geographical isolation and scattered islands present challenges in providing uniform educational access, but significant progress has been made in improving literacy.
 
• The islands are known for their rich biodiversity and indigenous tribal communities.

questions.question: According to the census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest percentage of rural population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, **Bihar recorded the highest percentage of rural population** among all Indian states.
 
• Approximately **88.7% of Bihar's total population** resides in rural areas, making it the most rural state in India.
 
• This high rural population is attributed to the state's predominantly agrarian economy and lack of significant urbanization.
 
• Other states with high rural population percentages include Uttar Pradesh, Assam, and Odisha, but **Bihar leads in terms of proportion**.
 
• The rural population in India as a whole was recorded at **68.84% in the 2011 Census**, highlighting the country's rural demographic dominance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rural Population:**

 
 
• Rural population refers to people living in villages and smaller settlements as opposed to urban areas (cities and towns).
 
• Rural areas in India are characterized by low population density, reliance on agriculture, and limited infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Census of India 2011:**
 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years and provides comprehensive data on population, literacy, employment, and living conditions.
 
• In 2011, the total population of India was recorded at **1.21 billion**, with 68.84% living in rural areas and 31.16% in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization in India:**
 
 
• Urbanization refers to the process by which rural areas transform into urban settlements through industrialization and modernization.
 
• India's urbanization rate is increasing, with significant migration to cities for better employment, education, and healthcare opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Agrarian Economy of Bihar:**
 
 
• Bihar's economy is heavily reliant on agriculture, with crops like rice, wheat, and maize being staples.
 
• The lack of significant industrialization has contributed to the state's high rural population percentage.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is 'NOT' correct about "Manures”?

options.text: They can be prepared in the fields
They do not provide humus to soil
They are relatively less rich in plant nutrients

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They do not provide humus to soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manures are organic substances that are used to improve soil fertility and crop productivity.**
 
• They can be prepared in the fields by decomposing plant and animal waste, or can be obtained from livestock farms or composting facilities.
 
• Manures are relatively less rich in plant nutrients compared to chemical fertilizers, but they provide a range of micronutrients and organic matter that are beneficial for plant growth.
 
• Manures also help to improve soil structure, water-holding capacity, and microbial activity, which in turn support healthy plant growth.
 
• Humus is a dark, organic substance that is formed by the decomposition of plant and animal matter in soil. It is a key component of soil fertility as it helps to retain moisture, nutrients, and carbon, and provides a habitat for soil organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• They can be prepared in the fields: It is correct as manures can be prepared in the fields by using techniques such as pit composting, vermicomposting, or green manuring.
 
• They do not provide humus to soil: It is incorrect as manures do provide humus to soil, which is a crucial component of soil health and fertility.
 
• They are relatively less rich in plant nutrients: It is correct as manures are relatively less concentrated in plant nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium compared to chemical fertilizers.
 
• They are natural substance: It is correct as manures are natural substances that are derived from plant and animal sources.

questions.question: Which of the following iron and steel plants is located in Jharkhand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bokaro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bokaro Steel Plant** is located in Bokaro, Jharkhand, and is one of the largest steel plants in India.
 
• It was established in **1964** with the collaboration of the Soviet Union and is operated by **Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)**.
 
• Bokaro Steel Plant is known for producing high-quality flat products such as hot-rolled, cold-rolled, and galvanized steel.
 
• It is strategically located in Jharkhand, which is rich in iron ore, coal, and other raw materials essential for steel production.
 
• The plant plays a significant role in India's industrial development and supports various sectors such as automotive, construction, and infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron and Steel Industry in India**

 
 
• India is the second-largest producer of crude steel in the world, as of 2023.
 
• The iron and steel industry is a core sector, contributing significantly to the economy and industrial development.
 
• Major steel plants in India include Tata Steel (Jamshedpur), Rourkela Steel Plant, and Bhilai Steel Plant.
 
 
 
• **Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)**
 
 
• SAIL is one of the largest steel-making companies in India, owned by the Government of India.
 
• It operates several integrated steel plants, including Bokaro, Rourkela, Bhilai, Durgapur, and Burnpur.
 
 
 
• **Raw Materials for Steel Production**
 
 
• Iron ore, coal, and limestone are the primary raw materials used in steel manufacturing.
 
• Jharkhand, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh are the major regions in India rich in these resources.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Steel Industry**
 
 
• The steel industry is crucial for infrastructure development, including bridges, buildings, railways, and power plants.
 
• It also supports the growth of ancillary industries such as automotive, machinery, and shipbuilding.

questions.question: Punjab state is rich in which natural resource from the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fertile soil**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fertile soil** is one of the major natural resources of Punjab.
 
• Punjab is known for its rich and fertile alluvial soil, which is highly conducive for agriculture.
 
• This fertile soil has made Punjab one of the leading agricultural states in India, producing significant quantities of wheat, rice, and other crops.
 
• The state's agricultural productivity is a key contributor to India's food grain production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Punjab** is often referred to as the "Granary of India" or "India's Breadbasket" due to its high agricultural output.
 
• The state benefits from an extensive irrigation system, primarily sourced from the rivers Sutlej, Beas, and Ravi.
 
• Punjab's agriculture sector plays a crucial role in ensuring food security for the nation.
 
• In addition to fertile soil, Punjab also has a well-developed infrastructure for the distribution and marketing of agricultural produce.
 
• The Green Revolution in India significantly boosted Punjab's agricultural productivity in the 1960s and 1970s.
 
• Punjab's farmers are known for their progressive farming techniques and adoption of modern agricultural practices.

questions.question: Which state in India has the highest population density as per the 2011 census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bihar has the **highest population density** among all Indian states as per the 2011 Census, with a density of **1,106 persons per square kilometer**.
 
• It is followed by West Bengal (1,028 persons per square kilometer) and Kerala (860 persons per square kilometer).
 
• The population density is calculated as the **number of people living per unit area of land**, typically per square kilometer.
 
• Bihar's high population density is attributed to factors like **limited land area**, high fertility rates, and a large rural population dependent on agriculture.
 
• Despite its high population density, Bihar's per capita income remains **lower than the national average**, indicating socio-economic challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density:** It is a key demographic metric used to measure the concentration of population in a specific geographic area. High density often results in resource constraints.
 
• **2011 Census of India:** The 2011 Census is the 15th Census conducted in India, providing data on population size, density, literacy rates, and other socio-economic indicators.
 
• **Low Density States:** Arunachal Pradesh has the **lowest population density** among Indian states, with only 17 persons per square kilometer as per the 2011 Census.
 
• **Urbanization Impact:** High population density is typically associated with urban areas, but in Bihar, it is seen even in rural regions due to its agrarian economy and limited industrialization.
 
• **Future Trends:** Population density is expected to increase in states like Bihar, making it crucial to address challenges in infrastructure, healthcare, and education to ensure sustainable development.
